sources.entry: Lila - Ad-less chess server powering lichess.org, with official iOS and Android client apps. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Scala

summary.one_liner: Lila is the open-source, ad-free chess server that powers lichess.org, written in Scala 3 with a TypeScript web client.
summary.what_it_does: Lila is a realtime online chess game server with a search engine, computer analysis distributed with fishnet, tournaments, simuls, forums, teams, a tactic trainer, a mobile app, and a shared analysis board. The server is built in Scala 3 on a modified Play 2.8 framework, using scalatags for templating and Pekko streams for asynchronous handling. Pure chess logic lives in the scalachess submodule. WebSocket connections are handled by a separate server that communicates over redis. The web client is written in TypeScript with snabbdom and Sass. The README says MongoDB stores more than 12 billion games, indexed by elasticsearch, and that all rated games are published as a free PGN database. It also mentions a public HTTP API that others may use.
use_cases: Running a self-hosted online chess site
Studying chess engine analysis of games
Building apps on the Lichess HTTP API
Training tactics with a puzzle trainer
Downloading the Lichess PGN game database
notable: Ad-less chess server that runs lichess.org itself
Computer analysis distributed across volunteer machines via fishnet
Full web UI available in more than 140 languages through community translation
Publishes all rated games as a free PGN database
Includes a mobile app along with the web client
caveats: Setting up a development environment is described only by reference to the project Wiki; the README gives no detailed steps
Older browsers are not supported (Firefox 100+, Chrome 100+, Edge 100+, Opera 97+, Safari 14+)
Production architecture depends on several services (MongoDB, elasticsearch, redis, a separate WebSocket server), so a full deployment is heavy
